problem: For x>=-b, the function f(x)=a sqrt(x+b), where a and b are positive constants. The graph passes through (1,6) and (10,12). What is f(25)?

bad.why: Dividing the two radical equations, squaring, and solving for b and a by hand takes several steps with radicals.

algebraFirst.description: Writes 6=a sqrt(1+b) and 12=a sqrt(10+b), divides and squares to get (10+b)/(1+b)=4, solves b=2 and a=2sqrt(3), then evaluates f(25).

explanationNotes: Explain that the two points act as a tiny table for f, so Desmos can find a and b at once by fitting f's formula to them. a comes out as a messy decimal (2sqrt(3), about 3.464), which is fine: f(25) is evaluated from the fitted function and comes out exactly 18.
notes: Original variant of Bedrock Prep's hard 'Radical Models' category. Dividing squared values gives (10+b)/(1+b)=4, hence b=2 and a=2sqrt(3); f(25)=2sqrt(3)*sqrt(27)=18. A Desmos fit should use the original two points and show the target evaluation. Source category: https://www.bedrockprep.com/problems
